demo.note: Self-test on The Cartographer of Echoes.

full_work.title: The Cartographer of Echoes
full_work.complete_text:
MARA. This valley isn't on any map. The compass spins here.
SURVEYOR. Then we map it. Every valley can be mapped.
ECHO. [from nowhere] Can it?
KEEPER. [stepping forward] This valley exists only in reflection. Map it, and you unmake it.
MARA. But my commission - my whole life is mapping!
KEEPER. Some places are kept by being unknown. Will you trade wonder for paper?
SURVEYOR. Mara - think of the fame.
MARA. [long pause] ...No. Some echoes are not for charting.
ECHO. Thank you.
MARA. [tearing the page] Let it stay unmapped. Let it stay.
KEEPER. Then you are its keeper now, too.
ALL. [softly] Some places live by being left alone.

ANSEL. Eight bells for the drowned cathedral. The ninth - I cannot cast it. It rings itself.
APPRENTICE. Master, bells don't ring themselves.
TIDE. [rising] Don't they?
CHOIR. [distant singing] Ring us home, bell-founder.

VIV. I forge love letters for a living. Beautiful lies, beautifully written.
THEO. [entering] I need a love letter. To myself. From someone who doesn't exist.
VIV. That's... unusually honest, for a liar.
THEO. I've forgotten what it feels like to be loved. I thought a letter might remind me.
VIV. [writing] 'Dear Theo - ' No. Too formal. 'My dearest - ' Too much. [pause] Tell me something true about you.
THEO. I'm afraid of the dark. I hum when I cook. I miss my mother.
VIV. [writing faster] There. Read it.
THEO. [reading, tears] This is... this is the truest thing anyone's ever written me.
VIV. Then it's not a forgery anymore.
THEO. Viv - will you write to me? As yourself?
VIV. I thought you'd never ask. [She begins: 'My dearest Theo - ']
ALL. The truest letters are the ones we almost didn't send.

STAR. [sneezing] I can't go on. The show - someone must -

BRAM. Forty years I've kept this light. And cataloged every book ever read aloud in it.
INSPECTOR. The light's automated now, Bram. You're retired. The books go to storage.
BOOKS. [as if whispering] Not storage. Please.
BRAM. These books kept me company through forty years of storms. They've earned the light.
INSPECTOR. Sentiment doesn't run lighthouses.
LIGHT. [flickering] Doesn't it?
BRAM. [opening a book, reading aloud] Then listen. One last story, for the light.
[He reads. The light steadies, burns brighter.]
INSPECTOR. That's... that's not possible.
BRAM. The books kept the keeper. Now they'll keep the ships. Light or no light.

GARDENER. You've got a heap of kitchen scraps, sire. That's a start.
COURTIER. [sniffing] Sire, this is beneath you. Literally. It's compost.
ROWAN. Then I shall be the Compost King! Bring me your peels, your grounds, your rot!

GARDENER. See? The heap heats itself. It asks nothing and gives everything.

NINA. [red pen] 'He went to the store, irregardless.' Honestly.
GHOST. [appearing] Don't - don't change that.
NINA. You're - you're a ghost. In a manuscript. Being copyedited.
GHOST. I died mid-sentence. Literally. The sentence was wrong, and so was I.
NINA. If I fix the grammar... what happens to you?
GHOST. Try it. Change one comma of my life.
NINA. [changing a comma] ...Did you - did you just smile?
GHOST. That comma was the day I didn't call my brother. Now I did.
NINA. [putting down the pen] Some errors shouldn't be corrected. Some should be forgiven.
GHOST. Leave the manuscript as it is. But thank you - for reading closely.
ALL. Punctuation can't save us. But attention might.

ANA. Our village governs by the hives. The bees decide. It's worked for a hundred years.
COUNCIL. But the queen is dead! The hive is queenless! What do we do?
QUEEN. [silence]
SWARM. [restless buzzing]
ANA. [listening] They're saying... we must choose. A new queen - or a new way.
COUNCIL. Vote? Debate? Filibuster?
ANA. Or trust. Watch: the workers are already raising a new queen. They knew before we did.
SWARM. [settling, harmonious]
ANA. The parliament of bees has ruled. Our job is just to listen.

ELI. Fifty years I've threaded this projector. Film is truth - twenty-four truths a second.
EXECUTIVE. We're going digital, Eli. Tonight's the last reel. Literally.
FILMS. [flickering to life on their own]
PROJECTOR. [running with no one threading it]
ELI. The films - they're projecting themselves!
EXECUTIVE. That's impossible. That's... beautiful.
FILMS. [showing: audiences laughing, crying, fifty years of Saturday nights]
ELI. They don't want to go. Neither do I.
EXECUTIVE. [quietly] ...Keep the projector. We'll keep the films. Some truths need sprocket holes.
ELI. [threading one last reel] Then let's watch something wonderful.
ALL. The light through film is the light through time.

FAY. Welcome to the Patience Exchange! Patience futures are up! Virtue bonds steady!
FLOOR. [chaotic shouting] Buy! Sell! Wait! No, wait - !

LARK. Forty years he tinkered. Forty years of gears and springs and 'almost, my love, almost.'
NEIGHBOR. And now you'll finish it? The impossible machine?
MACHINE. [half-built, silent]
BLUEPRINT. [covered in notes: 'almost!']
